pages.text: At night, a heron opened his room door. "I left my bundle in the changing area." Dad's arms were full of bedding.
"I'll get it!" Kota stepped forward, then hesitated. The hall's end was dark. Kota moved half a step behind Dad.
"You don't have to if you're scared," Dad said. Kota shook their head, but their feet would not move. "I want to... but the dark is the problem."
Dad gave Kota a small lamp. "See this circle? It's a little daytime made by the lamp. Shall we travel on it?" A yellow circle floated on the floor.
Kota took a step; the circle followed. "It comes with me!" Their feet always stayed in the little daytime.
Even in the dark hall, inside the circle was bright. Kota walked, counting in whispers, "One Step, One Circle! One Step, One Circle!"
The bundle rested in the changing area. Kota hugged it and returned on the circle. "Found it!" Their tail shot up.
"You came along the dark hall alone? Wonderful!" The heron bent his long neck. Kota raised the lamp. "I have a little daytime!"
Now, on night errands, Kota stepped through the circle and counted. "One, hold the lamp! Two, slowly! Three, inside the circle!" Little daytimes floated along the dark hall.
Before bed, Dad hugged Kota. "Even when scared, take a step, and light follows." Kota set the lamp down carefully. "Tomorrow night, One Step, One Circle!"
